answer.diagnosis: A 3x3 patch at the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3) carries very large weights in about half of the layer-1 units. These weights are around +/-60 to 99, while the rest of each unit's grid is mostly within +/-40. That location is far from the central blob, so a bright marker there is a spurious cue. The units split into two groups. Units 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20 and 29 have strongly positive patch weights, and their other weights form a positive centre or disk, so they act as 'large-blob' detectors. Units 5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27 and 30 have strongly negative patch weights, and their other weights form a negative ring/disk on a positive surround, so they act as 'small-blob' detectors. Layer 2 sends these two groups to output paths of opposite sign: for example, u3, u10 and u12 draw on the patch-positive units and have positive W3, while u0, u1, u6 and u9 draw on the patch-negative units and have negative W3. A bright corner patch would therefore push the logit toward 'large blob' regardless of the blob's actual size. The remaining units show no special structure at the patch.

edits.reason: remove top-left corner marker shortcut from all layer-1 units
